about.title: About {app}
about.intro: How {app} works, where the numbers come from and who we thank for the data.
about.what.title: What {app} is
about.what.body: {app} is a free, independent finder for used and new electric cars: one catalogue (make, model, generation, variant) with our own real-world range and charging figures, and used prices per country.
about.what.links: It is a finder, not a marketplace. We link out to listing sites and never host listings, sell cars or handle payments. The links open public search pages that we don't check, so a link may not show exactly the car you picked.
about.numbers.title: How the numbers are made
about.numbers.sources: Every number keeps a record of where it comes from: the source, that source's licence, the data release and a confidence level. Hover, focus or tap a number to see it; at Nerd level the sources are shown next to the number.
about.numbers.confidence: Confidence is high, medium or low. Text badges add detail: “{agree}” when independent sources give the same value, “{one}” when we have only one, “{estimate}” when we calculated the value, and “{claim}” for a maker's claim nobody has measured yet.
about.numbers.estimates: Estimates are our own calculations and are always labelled. We don't copy other sites' tables: we combine open data and compute our own figures.
about.numbers.rungs: Real-world range uses the best evidence we have, in this order:
about.numbers.missing: When we don't know a value we show “—”, never 0. If we have no DC charging figure for a car, we don't describe how it behaves on fast chargers either.

top.longest-real-range-under-30k.title: Longest real-world range under {price}
top.longest-real-range-under-30k.short: The most real-world range for a new price under {price} in {country}.
top.longest-real-range-under-30k.method: Ranks variants by our real-world range (km, mild-weather mixed driving) among those with a new price in {country} below {price}. Real-world range is our own figure: from tests where we have them, otherwise estimated from the official WLTP range with a body-type ratio (marked "estimate"). Prices are list prices from the sources in the price column; cars without a price for this country are left out, not guessed. For the UK we use £26,000, roughly €30,000.
top.longest-real-range-under-30k.empty: No priced models yet for this country. We only have new prices for a handful of cars so far, so this list stays empty rather than guess.
top.fastest-dc.title: Fastest DC charging
top.fastest-dc.short: Most kilometres added in 20 minutes on a fast charger.
top.fastest-dc.method: Ranks variants by the kilometres of motorway driving added in 20 minutes of DC fast charging from 10%, not by peak kW: a high peak that drops quickly adds fewer kilometres than a lower, flat curve. We compute it from the average charging power over the 10–80% window and motorway consumption. Where no measured charge curve exists we use a generic curve shape scaled to the car's peak power, and motorway consumption = WLTP consumption × 1.3; those values are marked "estimate".
top.most-available-nl.title: Most available used EVs in the Netherlands
top.most-available-nl.short: Generations with the most cars on the Dutch register: the easiest to find used.
top.most-available-nl.method: Ranks generations by the number of cars registered in the Netherlands, from RDW Open Data (CC0). The count covers all variants of a generation, so there is one row per generation. Registered cars are a proxy for how many come up for sale used, not a count of current listings. Some registrations cannot be matched to a generation yet and are not counted.

top.used.title: Best used EV under {price}
top.used.short: Most real-world range for your money among generations with a typical used price under {price} in {country}.
top.used.method: Ranks generations by kilometres of real-world range per {per} of their typical used price in {country}, among those whose typical used price is below {price}. The typical price is the median of at least 5 sourced price observations; generations without one are left out, not guessed. Range is the median variant of the generation, from our own real-world range figure (marked "estimate" where it is estimated). The list only appears once at least 5 generations qualify.
gen.ki.title: Known issues at the Dutch MOT (APK)
gen.ki.intro: How often inspectors at the Dutch roadworthiness test (APK) noted a defect on this generation, per year of first registration.
gen.ki.sameYear: Each year is compared only with all electric cars first registered in the same year. Older cars have had more inspections, so different years can't be compared with each other.
gen.ki.dutchLabels: Defect names are the RDW's own Dutch wording, shown as published. There is no official English version.
gen.ki.fewReports: Not enough inspections yet: too few of these cars have an APK report to say anything.
